items.title: Anwar condemns international community’s failure to end Palestinian suffering
items.summary: BANGI, Oct 14 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has condemned the failure of the international order to address the suffering of the Palestinian people. “We talk of democracy, whose democracy? We talk of human rights, which human?

items.title: Student struck and killed by car while crossing road in Miri
items.summary: MIRI, Oct 14 — A 16-year-old student was killed after being struck by a car while crossing the road near SMK Luar Bandar Miri in Bekenu on Tuesday. Miri police chief ACP Mohd Farhan Lee Abdullah said the accident occurred at about 1.10pm when a car driven by a 46-year-old local woman, travelling from Miri towards Bakong, allegedly struck the student. Mohd Farhan said the impact damaged the front-left section of the car, while the driver was unhurt.

items.title: Finance Ministry: RM17.15b in excess tax refunds paid to individuals, companies as of Sept 30
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — The government has settled tax overpayment refunds amounting to RM17.15 billion, involving 3.23 million taxpayer cases, for the period up to September 30, 2026. According to the Ministry of Finance (MoF), this total included RM6.38 billion being refunded to 3.1 million individual taxpayers and RM8.95 billion being refunded to over 130,000 corporate taxpayers, including micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs). “The government is also committed to ensuring that outstanding refunds are fully settled promptly as part of efforts to enhance tax administration efficiency and safeguard taxpayers' rights, in line with the Madani government’s fiscal reform agenda,” the Ministry of Finance (MoF) said in a written reply published on the parliament website yesterday.

items.title: FBM KLCI opens higher on bargain-hunting, resilient domestic fundamental
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia opened higher on Wednesday, maintaining a cautious but positive tone, supported by continued bargain-hunting activities and resilient domestic fundamentals. At 9.10am, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) gained 4.50 points, or 0.27 per cent, to 1,627.85 from yesterday's close of 1,623.35. Turnover stood at 239.44 million units worth RM140.08 million.

items.title: Budget 2027: MPs welcome higher Sabah, Sarawak allocations, call for faster project delivery
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — The increased interim special grants and larger development allocations for Sabah and Sarawak are expected to strengthen development in both states, with Members of Parliament (MPs) hoping this will be followed by a finalised special grant formula and more effective project implementation. Datuk Mohd Kurniawan Naim Moktar (BN-Kinabatangan) urged the government to explain the latest status of negotiations on the formula granting Sabah the right to receive 40 per cent of the net revenue derived by the Federal Government from the state. “This is not just a matter of additional allocations; it involves constitutional responsibility and fiscal relations between the federal government and the Sabah government.

items.title: Dollar languishes as focus turns to CPI, Fed speakers
items.summary: The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies, edged 0.02 per cent lower to 102.16, following a 0.35 per cent slide on Tuesday. The euro rose 0.04 per cent to US$1.1203. The yen was little changed at 158.32 per dollar, and sterling rose 0.03 per cent to US$1.3256.

items.title: Perak to prioritise local water needs before supplying Penang - Exco
items.summary: IPOH: The Perak state government has assured that the state's domestic, industrial and agricultural water needs will be prioritised before any surplus is supplied to Penang under the Bulk Water Supply Agreement (BWSA). Perak Infrastructure, Energy, Water and Transport Committee chairman Datuk Seri Mohammad Nizar Jamaluddin said the approach was crucial to ensuring a sustainable water supply in the state, particularly in anticipation of rising demand in the years ahead. The agreement, signed between Khazanah Air Perak Sdn Bhd (KAP) and Penang Water Supply Corporation (PBAPP), targets the initial delivery of treated water in the first quarter of 2032.

items.title: Finance Ministry: Malaysians under 30 rack up RM5.4b in BNPL transactions in first half of 2026
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — Young people aged 30 and below recorded 65.9 million Buy Now, Pay Later (BNPL) transactions worth RM5.4 billion in the first half of 2026, accounting for 37.9 per cent of total BNPL transactions in Malaysia, according to the Ministry of Finance (MoF). In a written reply published on the parliament website yesterday, the MoF said the total number of BNPL transactions in Malaysia during that period was 173.9 million, valued at RM14.7 billion, with youths contributing 36.7 per cent of the total transaction value. As of June 30, 2026, the outstanding BNPL financing balance for this demographic stood at RM2.4 billion, while non-performing financing amounted to RM96.8 million, or 4.0 per cent of the outstanding balance.

items.title: Close, but not caviar: Sushi King wins tax dispute over imported fish roe
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — The seasoned fish eggs commonly served on sushi rolls are culinary garnishes rather than luxury caviar substitutes under customs law, the High Court has ruled. Judge Norliza Othman dismissed an appeal by the Customs Department director-general against a Customs Appeal Tribunal decision that favoured restaurant chain Sushi King Sdn Bhd regarding the classification of imported tobiko (flying fish roe), masago (capelin roe), and frozen mentaiko (pollock roe), NST reported. “Fish roe is a wide, all-encompassing term used to describe fish eggs, but not all fish roe is caviar or a caviar substitute.

items.title: Oil prices climb as traders weigh Saudi supply risk, Russian diesel flow
items.summary: TOKYO:Oil prices climbed on Wednesday as traders weighed supply risks from fighting between Yemen's Iran-allied Houthis and Saudi Arabia against the prospect of increased diesel exports from Russia. Brent crude futures rose 89 cents, or eight-tenths of a per cent, to US$106.58 a barrel by 0030 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures gained 80 cents, or nine-tenths of a per cent, to US$94.94. Brent fell 0.9 per cent on Tuesday, while WTI rose 0.4 per cent.

items.title: Budget 2027: Technology adoption, business growth key to higher wages, says minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — The adoption of technology and business scaling can boost company productivity and enhance the ability to share the gains of growth with employees through wage increases, said Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir. He noted that efforts to raise productivity to support wage growth must involve not only employees but also the capabilities of employers. Akmal Nasrullah said the adoption of technology and financing that supports business scaling are among the ways to strengthen the capabilities of micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs).

items.title: Budget 2027: Kelantan, Terengganu, Perlis, Kedah, Sabah, Sarawak get RM21.26b development allocation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — The government has allocated RM21.26 billion in development expenditure to six underdeveloped states under Budget 2027, with the distribution taking into account the different needs of each state, said Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir. He said the six states are Kelantan, Terengganu, Perlis, Kedah, Sabah and Sarawak, with the allocation also reflecting the commitment to infrastructure development and the implementation of previously announced projects. Akmal Nasrullah said development spending is not only aimed at driving economic growth but also at bridging the development gap between states, including those that are lagging behind.

items.title: 4,289 bullying cases recorded in schools from March to August, says Fadhlina
items.summary: Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said the cases, including incidents in hostels, comprised 2,480 involving physical bullying, 1,386 verbal bullying, 243 non-verbal bullying and 180 cyberbullying. In response, she said, the Education Ministry has stepped up hostel monitoring through expanded closed-circuit television (CCTV) coverage, additional assistant wardens and safety audits. The ministry had also audited hostel safety at 850 schools, with follow-up efforts this year through the Student Safety and Well-being Survey (TKKM) and In-Situ Guidance: Student Safety and Well-being (BKKM).

items.title: Malaysian police trace syndicate behind 521kg syabu seizure in Laos on jet from Subang
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) have identified a syndicate and several individuals believed to be linked to the arrests and drug seizure at Luang Prabang International Airport, Laos, earlier this month. Bukit Aman Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said investigators had recorded statements from several witnesses, including a Malaysian who acted as a broker who arranged the charter of the aircraft involved. Hussein said the case was being handled by the NCID’s Special Investigation Unit under Sections 34 and 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, relating to abetment or preparation in Malaysia for drug trafficking offences committed abroad.

items.title: [UPDATED] Police to send team to Japan after five Malaysians arrested over 5kg cocaine hidden in shoe insoles
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police will send an investigation team to Japan following the arrest of five Malaysians after 5kg of cocaine was found hidden in their shoe insoles at Haneda Airport in Tokyo on Oct 10. He said Japanese authorities were also investigating the source of the cocaine and working to identify syndicate members and international drug trafficking networks. "Japanese authorities have informed NCID about the arrest of two Malaysian men and three women at Haneda Airport on Oct 10.

items.title: Three teens injured after flag strikes high-voltage line during Alor Setar procession
items.summary: ALOR SETAR, Oct 14 — Three teenage boys were injured by an electric shock after a flag they were carrying during a vegetable temple procession in Mergong, near here, tonight allegedly came into contact with a high-voltage power line. Mergong Vegetable Temple Association Secretary Chah Boon Chuan said the incident, which occurred at about 9pm, resulted in two 17-year-old victims and one 16-year-old being rushed to Sultanah Bahiyah Hospital (HSB) here. “The incident happened while thousands of procession participants were marching along the main road in the area before one of the flags allegedly hit the power line.

items.title: Haze continues hitting Johor, Selangor, KL hard: API 177 in Pasir Gudang
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — Air quality deteriorated further across the country this morning, with 27 monitoring stations recording unhealthy air pollutant index (API) readings as haze intensified across the central and southern regions of Peninsular Malaysia. Another 40 stations logged moderate air quality, only one recorded good air quality, and none crossed into the very unhealthy or hazardous categories. Selangor accounted for five unhealthy stations.

items.title: Kelantan Social Welfare Dept: Husbands can also be victims of domestic violence
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Oct 14 — Domestic violence does not only involve husbands abusing their wives, but can also involve wives or other family members abusing husbands, said Kelantan Social Welfare Department (JKM) director Che Samsuzuki Che Noh. He said the issue must be taken seriously as violence within the family could result in serious injuries, death or other criminal acts if left unchecked. In this regard, he said JKM would continue working with the Kelantan State Women’s Development Office, the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) and relevant agencies to raise public awareness of domestic violence and the assistance available to victims.

items.title: 27 stations record unhealthy API readings across Peninsular Malaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 27 air quality monitoring stations nationwide recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 8am today, all in Peninsular Malaysia. Kuala Terengganu recorded the highest moderate reading nationwide at 97. No monitoring stations recorded very unhealthy or hazardous air quality.

items.title: Govt may allow refugees to fill labour gaps in 3D sectors
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government may allow registered refugees to fill labour shortages in the 3D (dirty, dangerous and difficult) sectors to reduce Malaysia's dependence on foreign workers. He said the government intended to identify refugees of working age who had passed screening to assess their potential to meet the country's workforce needs. "There are five economic sectors that require workers.

items.title: ‘False report’: Indonesian student, not Malaysian, held in Tanjung Balai 4kg syabu case, says Bukit Aman
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) denied reports in a local newspaper and on social media claiming a Malaysian university student was arrested for smuggling over four kilogrammes of syabu in Tanjung Balai, Indonesia, on October 10. Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said investigations found that the suspect arrested by the republic’s authorities is a 21-year-old Indonesian man. Hussein said the drugs were obtained from a syndicate in Malaysia before being smuggled out.

items.title: 'No caviar here': Sushi King wins Customs dispute
items.summary: The High Court has ruled that tobiko (flying fish roe), masago (capelin roe) and frozen mentaiko (pollock roe) imported by restaurant chain Sushi King Sdn Bhd are not caviar substitutes, despite being seasoned, coloured and preserved. On Oct 8, 2020, Sushi King submitted three applications to the Customs Department seeking tariff rulings for the imported fish roe. The department classified the products as caviar substitutes, which attract an 8 per cent import duty.

items.title: Sabah diesel aid covers 52,133 pickup, SUV owners under Budi Diesel scheme
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — A total of 52,133 owners of diesel vehicles such as pickups and sport utility vehicles (SUVs) in Sabah have been approved for an additional 100 litres of diesel under the Budi Madani Diesel (Budi Diesel) programme as of October 12, 2026, said the Ministry of Finance (MoF). The ministry said the additional eligibility criteria take into account the higher diesel consumption needs, particularly among rural residents, small traders, farmers and those who use diesel vehicles to generate income. MoF noted that the government implemented the diesel subsidy targeting reform through Budi Diesel in phases beginning June 27, 2026, before expanding its implementation nationwide on July 1, 2026.

items.title: Violent Kota Damansara thunderstorm: Viral clip shows wind lifting car at toll plaza (VIDEO)
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — A dramatic video capturing the terrifying moment violent storm winds appeared to lift a car and toss it into another vehicle near a toll plaza in Kota Damansara has gone viral on social media. The footage, shared online at around 6.30pm yesterday, shows what witnesses described as a waterspout or freak whirlwind striking motorists queuing along the toll lanes amid blinding rain and howling gusts. In the clip, the powerful vortex lifts the rear of a stationary car waiting to approach the toll barrier, shoving it forcefully into an adjacent vehicle.

items.title: Creating a senior-friendly tourism ecosystem
items.summary: LETTER: At what age is someone officially considered as a senior citizen - 55, 60, 62 or 65? Golden Screen Cinemas, for example, offers senior citizen rates to patrons aged 55 years old and above. Should Malaysia therefore lower all senior discounts to 55?

items.title: Ringgit opens marginally higher against US dollar on weaker DXY
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened marginally higher against the US dollar on Wednesday, supported by a weaker US Dollar Index (DXY) as investors reassessed the outlook for US interest rates following signals that the Federal Reserve may adopt a less aggressive monetary policy stance. At 8am, the ringgit rose to 4.0830/0880 against the greenback from Tuesday's close of 4.0835/0880. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the DXY fell 0.40 per cent to 102.810 points after US Federal Reserve Bank of New York President John Williams indicated that the Fed Funds Rate may not be raised in 2027, as inflation is expected to ease gradually towards the two per cent target.

items.title: In Dewan Rakyat today: Alibaba licences, Gaza and troubled housing project among focus
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — Legislation to curb “Alibaba” licensing practices, Malaysia’s diplomatic efforts on Gaza and the fate of an abandoned housing project are among the key issues expected to be raised in the Dewan Rakyat today. According to the Order Paper, Syahredzan Johan (PH-Bangi) will ask the Economy Minister about the status of drafting the Anti-Rent-Seeking Act and the timeline for its tabling in Parliament to curb “Alibaba” licensing practices. The Dewan Rakyat will then continue debating the Supply Bill 2027 at the policy stage, following the tabling of Budget 2027 by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also Finance Minister, last Friday.

items.title: Immigration identifies 224 hotspots linked to undocumented migrants
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Immigration Department has identified 224 hotspots nationwide linked to the presence and activities of foreigners, including illegal settlements and overcrowded rental houses. Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said other locations included workers' quarters at construction sites and business premises dominated by foreigners. He said these locations required close attention and enforcement monitoring.

items.title: US high court to decide if cooking qualifies as terror support
items.summary: WASHINGTON: Does cooking for members of a Nigerian separatist group amount to providing "material support" for terrorism? That's the thorny question facing the conservative-majority US Supreme Court. In a brief order Tuesday, the Supreme Court agreed to hear the Trump administration's bid to reinstate the ruling that denied asylum to a Nigerian man who was deported for having provided material support to a terrorist group.

items.title: Ali Baba licences, Gaza and troubled housing project among Dewan Rakyat's focus today
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Legislation to curb "Ali Baba" licensing practices, Malaysia's diplomatic efforts to sustain the Gaza ceasefire and the fate of a troubled housing project are among the key issues expected to be raised in the Dewan Rakyat today. After the question-and-answer session, the Dewan Rakyat will consider a motion by the prime minister to appoint members of parliament to the Parliamentary Services Council. Under the motion, two government MPs, Ramkarpal Singh (PH-Bukit Gelugor) and Datuk Seri Hasni Mohammad (BN-Simpang Renggam), and two opposition MPs, Datuk Seri Dr Ronald Kiandee (PN-Beluran) and Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan (PN-Kota Bharu), will be nominated to the council under Section 3(2)(f) of the Parliamentary Services Act 2025.

items.title: Singapore central bank keeps monetary policy unchanged
items.summary: SINGAPORE: Singapore's central bank on Wednesday kept its monetary policy settings unchanged. The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) said it would maintain the prevailing rate of appreciation in its exchange rate-based policy band, known as the Singapore dollar nominal effective exchange rate, or S$NEER. All 10 analysts polled by Reuters had expected the MAS to tighten monetary policy.

items.title: Gold subdued ahead of US inflation data, Warsh remarks
items.summary: NEW YORK: Gold prices edged lower on Tuesday, while investors awaited key US inflation data and remarks from the Federal Reserve chair due later this week to gauge the outlook on monetary policy. Spot gold fell 0.3 per cent to US$4,157.90 per ounce by 2.15pm EDT (1815 GMT). US gold futures for December settled down 0.3 per cent at US$4,177.30 per ounce.

items.title: US stocks dip ahead of inflation data as tech sell-off hits Asia
items.summary: NEW YORK: Wall Street stocks were mostly lower at the end of a choppy session Tuesday, digesting solid results from US banks and a pullback in Asian markets prompted by worries over the AI investment boom. While JPMorgan Chase missed analyst estimates, the US banking giant joined three other large US banks in reporting year-on-year profit increases that pointed to continued health in the US consumer. JPMorgan Chief Financial Officer Jeremy Barnum described US consumer spending as "sort of robust," adding that the consumer credit picture remains "quite resilient" despite persistent inflationary trends.

items.title: Oil prices settle mixed, focus on US-Russia diesel deal, Saudi Yemen attacks
items.summary: LONDON/SINGAPORE: Oil prices were mixed on Tuesday as hopes the US-Russia diesel deal could free up more supplies from Moscow offset attacks in Saudi Arabia and Yemen that could result in additional supply disruptions. US West Texas Intermediate crude futures rose 40 cents, or 0.4 per cent, to settle at US$94.14, the highest close for WTI since Sept 24. Russia was the world's third-biggest crude oil producer behind the US and Saudi Arabia in 2025, according to US energy data.

items.title: Fed Governor Cook's lawyer denounces Trump's latest attempt to remove her
items.summary: Earlier this month, Trump announced a fresh inquiry into Cook and the appointment of a three-person committee to hold a hearing. Cook's lawyers have said a fair hearing would show there was no legal basis for firing her. The earliest Cook could attend any hearing would be after the Fed's policy meeting scheduled for Dec 8-9, he wrote.

items.title: When haze can cloud our judgment
items.summary: MALAYSIANS should not have to become fire investigators to ask for cleaner air. Naming a company, blaming a farmer or condemning an entire industry may settle an argument in the comments section. Responsibility matters throughout.

items.title: Malaysia seeks Euro tech, talent and jobs as FTA deal nears June 2027 target
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia must turn European investments into a catalyst for technology transfer, skilled job creation and stronger local industries as it seeks to move up the global value chain amid intensifying US-China competition, economists said. Johari said Malaysia wanted European investments to facilitate technology transfer, develop highly skilled talent and create better-paying jobs as the country moves into its next phase of economic development. EU-Asean Business Council executive director Chris Humphrey said Malaysia could build on its existing attractiveness as a foreign direct investment (FDI)destination to draw more European companies into the country.

items.title: Prasarana ramps up efforts to improve LRT reliability
items.summary: PETALING JAYA: Prasarana Malaysia Bhd is stepping up efforts to improve Light Rail Transit (LRT) reliability through round-the-clock maintenance, closer supplier engagement and the introduction of 26 new train sets for the Kelana Jaya Line. Prasarana acting president and group chief executive officer Dr Prodyut Dutt acknowledged that the Kelana Jaya line had faced greater reliability challenges this year. On the Kelana Jaya line, that represents a deterioration of about 30 per cent," he said.

items.title: Saudi says Houthi attacks sparked Aramco fire, wounded four in Riyadh
items.summary: SANAA: Saudi Arabia said on Wednesday that an attack on an Aramco building in the kingdom's east sparked a "limited fire", while debris from intercepted Houthi missiles wounded four people in the capital, Riyadh. It came hours after the Saudi-led coalition battling Yemen's Houthis said it had intercepted several missiles on Tuesday evening, including over Riyadh. Earlier on Tuesday, the coalition struck oil sites across western Yemen in response to the deadliest attack on Saudi soil in years.

items.title: US targets network funneling IT earnings to North Korea
items.summary: WASHINGTON: Federal prosecutors said on Tuesday that they had made two arrests and seized more than 180 computers in an effort to dismantle an alleged North Korean scheme to profit from remote IT work based in the US. In a statement, the Department of Justice said it had searched "more than 40 suspected 'laptop farms' across Texas" that generated more than US$3 million for Pyongyang by deceiving US employers into hiring North Koreans. In April, two US nationals, Zhenxing Wang and Kejia Wang, were sentenced to 92 months and 108 months, respectively, for a "multi-year scheme that used the stolen identities of at least 80 US persons and generated more than US$5 million in illicit revenue" for the North Korean government.

items.title: Transboundary haze: Jakarta mulls Malaysia's offer to help
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Indonesia is carefully assessing Malaysia's offer of firefighting assistance, with thick smoke limiting visibility and complicating plans for aerial operations, the Indonesian embassy here said. The embassy said the Indonesian government was coordinating internally, with the National Disaster Management Agency leading efforts to determine what form of aid would be needed most. "Indonesia welcomes and deeply appreciates Malaysia's kind offer of assistance in addressing the current forest and land fires in Indonesia.

items.title: Social media, disappearing messages fuel drug mule recruitment [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Drug syndicates are exploiting social media and messaging platforms to recruit couriers and using disappearing messages to erase their digital trail and make it harder for authorities to uncover evidence. Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the recruitment of drug mules had evolved beyond face-to-face approaches, with syndicates taking advantage of digital platforms to identify and communicate with potential couriers. Syndicates were also exploiting disappearing message features, he said.

items.title: International drug rings eyeing other airports as KLIA steps up scrutiny [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: International drug syndicates are shifting their attention to other Malaysian airports as enforcement intensifies at the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA). Syndicates are now targeting Bayan Lepas International Airport in Penang, Kota Kinabalu International Airport in Sabah and airports in Ipoh, Perak, and Miri, Sarawak. Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said intelligence revealed that syndicates were looking for alternative routes.

items.title: Experts: Cut off market for stolen cables to cripple syndicates
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Shutting down the market for stolen cables by zeroing in on unscrupulous scrapyard operators could cripple cable theft syndicates disrupting critical infrastructure nationwide. Describing cable theft as economic sabotage, senior lawyer Kitson Foong said enforcement must go beyond arresting cable thieves and target scrap metal dealers who knowingly buy stolen cables. "Every stolen metre of cable has a buyer.

items.title: Cable thieves emerge from the shadows
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Once content with operating under cover of darkness, cable thieves are becoming increasingly brazen, stripping valuable copper from the nation's infrastructure in broad daylight — sometimes in full view of passing motorists and residents. Police also seized five cars, cable-cutting equipment and three sacks of burnt copper wires. Investigators believe the arrests solved several cable theft cases in Negri Sembilan, Selangor, Kedah and Melaka.

items.title: Multi-lane fast flow: What motorists need to know as Malaysia moves towards barrier-free tolling
items.summary: As part of that transition, two systems are now being introduced to motorists: PLUS’ JustGo and Touch ’n Go’s Titan Flow. JustGo is a digital toll payment system that uses automatic number plate recognition (ANPR) to identify a vehicle and charge the debit or credit card linked to the motorist’s account. — Picture by Sayuti Zainudin JustGo JustGo is essentially a camera-based toll payment system.

items.title: US fines Bank of America US$1.2 billion for anti-money laundering violations
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The US Treasury Department said on Tuesday that it was imposing penalties of more than US$1.2 billion on Bank of America, citing "violations of anti-money laundering and sanctions laws". The second-biggest US bank failed to properly report more than US$5 billion in "suspicious transactions", the department said. The overall charge involves US$1.2 billion assessed by the Treasury Department's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network.

items.title: Police: Two investigation papers opened over RM350,000 bribery claim against senior MACC officer
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — Two separate investigation papers have been opened into allegations that a senior Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) officer received a bribe of RM350,000 from an individual in 2017. Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department (CID) director Datuk M. Kumar said the investigations were initiated following a police report lodged over the matter, which had gone viral on several social media platforms. Kumar said the investigation is being conducted under Section 500 of the Penal Code for defamation, which carries a maximum penalty of two years’ jail, a fine, or both upon conviction.

items.title: Myanmar refugees convicted of offences must serve sentence in Malaysia before repatriation, says Saifuddin Nasution
items.summary: SUNGAI PETANI, Oct 13 — Myanmar refugees convicted of criminal offences must complete their sentences in this country before being repatriated to their home country. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said although the Myanmar government is prepared to accept back its citizens currently held in Immigration detention depots here, screening will be conducted first before such action is taken. “The Myanmar government has agreed to accept back its citizens who are here following our screening process, if our records show they were involved in legal violations, we will handle the legal proceedings first,” he said.

items.title: Anwar calls for stronger federal-state cooperation under National Covenant framework
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — The federal and state governments must strengthen cooperation under the proposed National Covenant framework to ensure more sustainable, equitable and balanced development, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. The proposed covenant aims to strengthen federal-state cooperation and promote more inclusive development and public well-being. “Amid global economic uncertainties, national growth projections and fluctuations in global oil prices, the budget must continue to protect the people, address the rising cost of living and take into account each state’s priorities, including border security, particularly in Sabah and Sarawak,” he said in a Facebook post today.

items.title: Cross-border haze to ease in two weeks as monsoon transition begins, says deputy minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — The cross-border haze that has affected Malaysia’s air quality since August 8 is expected to gradually subside over the next two weeks as wind patterns change, Deputy Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Syed Ibrahim Syed Noh said. He said Malaysia had entered the monsoon transition phase on October 9, with the northeast monsoon expected to begin towards the end of this month. Syed Ibrahim was responding to concerns raised by Khoo Poay Tiong (PH-Kota Melaka), who described the haze as a national crisis affecting public health, safety, the economy and public well-being.

items.title: Haze: Kedah schools to operate as usual tomorrow as API readings remain moderate
items.summary: ALOR SETAR, Oct 13 — All schools in Kedah will operate as usual tomorrow, with Air Pollutant Index (API) readings across the state remaining below 100 as of 2pm today. In a statement, the Kedah State Education Department (JPN) said any decisions on school closures or reopening due to the haze would be subject to the Education Ministry’s directives, based on JPN’s monitoring of daily API readings and local developments. “Kedah JPN will continue to monitor the situation and coordinate with the District Education Offices and schools to safeguard the health, safety and well-being of students and education personnel,” it added.

items.title: Home Ministry to seek details on five Malaysians held in Japan drug bust, says Saifuddin Nasution
items.summary: SUNGAI PETANI, Oct 13 — The Home Ministry will contact Japanese authorities to obtain accurate information on the arrest of Malaysians suspected of involvement in a drug case in Japan. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said he had instructed Bukit Aman Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan to act immediately to establish the facts. However, he said destinations in Japan, including Tokyo, were not included in the original list of hotspots.

items.title: Businessman sentenced to six months’ jail, ordered to pay RM5,000 for assaulting ex-girlfriend
items.summary: Magistrate Amira Sariaty Zainal imposed the sentence on Hoh Peng Onn, 47, after the defence failed to raise reasonable doubt at the end of the defence case. The accused must also pay RM5,000 in compensation to the victim, taking into account the trauma, injuries and emotional distress she suffered,” Amira Sariaty said. The court also ordered that Hoh serve an additional two months in jail if he failed to pay the compensation today.

items.title: Budget 2027: Malaysia’s 3.3pc fiscal deficit target achievable, says Tengku Zafrul
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — Malaysia is capable of achieving its fiscal deficit target of 3.3 per cent of gross domestic product (GDP) under Budget 2027, provided the assumptions underpinning the budget hold amid global economic and geopolitical uncertainties, said Datuk Seri Tengku Zafrul Abdul Aziz. He described Budget 2027 as a responsible budget that balances investment incentives with efforts to ensure that economic growth benefits a wider segment of Malaysians and businesses. On investment prospects, Tengku Zafrul said planned capital expenditure by government-linked investment companies (GLICs) and government-linked companies (GLCs) could generate positive spillover effects for the broader economy.

items.title: Senior govt agency official, company director remanded seven days in bribery probe
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — A senior official of a government agency and a company director have been remanded for seven days for allegedly soliciting and receiving bribes totalling about RM15,000. Magistrate Aliaa Anwar issued the remand order against both men, effective from today until Oct 19, following an application by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) at the Kuala Lumpur Magistrate’s Court this morning. Meanwhile, Kuala Lumpur MACC director Mohammad Zakkuan Talib, when contacted, confirmed the remand.

items.title: STAM and MUET examinations in Pahang to continue as planned despite haze
items.summary: KUANTAN, Oct 13 — The Sijil Tinggi Agama Malaysia (STAM) and Malaysian University English Test (MUET) examinations in Pahang will proceed as scheduled despite the haze. In a statement, the Pahang State Education Department (JPN) said the examinations would be conducted in accordance with the standard operating procedures (SOP) and safety measures in force. Pahang JPN will continue to monitor the situation in coordination with the three district education offices and relevant agencies to safeguard the health, safety and well-being of students and education personnel.

items.title: Teachers union: RM69b education allocation must bring real improvements to Malaysian schools
items.summary: West Malaysia Malay Teachers Union (KGMMB) president Dr Mohd Sobri Yusuf said the RM69 billion allocation, up from RM66.2 billion this year, should translate into meaningful improvements in schools, with its success measured by the actual benefits delivered to teachers and students. Mohd Sobri said the higher school maintenance allocation, which has doubled to RM2 billion, could deliver direct benefits to school communities, particularly in ensuring that learning facilities were safe and comfortable. Mohd Sobri said the recruitment of 200 teaching assistants for primary schools with large numbers of pupils could help reduce teachers’ workload, allowing them to focus more on teaching and students’ learning needs.

items.title: Fahmi proposes initiative to preserve speeches, writings of Malaysia’s founding leaders
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil today has proposed a national initiative to preserve and revive historical speeches and writings of Malaysia’s founding leaders for future generations. He said the initiative, inspired by the reprint of pioneering journalist J. Victor Morais’ Great Wisdom of the First Malaysians, could involve retrieving rare speeches, writings and historical accounts from archives. Fahmi said this at the launch of Great Wisdom of the First Malaysians – A Reprint of Selected Speeches by Pioneering Journalist J. Victor Morais here today.

items.title: Orang Asli children should not be denied documentation over parents’ marriage records, says National Registration Dept
items.summary: GUA MUSANG, Oct 13 — Orang Asli children should not be left without documentation because of issues involving their parents’ marriage records, said National Registration Department (JPN) director-general Datuk Badrul Hisham Alias. He said JPN would assess each case based on the facts, supporting documents and individual circumstances to determine the appropriate action, particularly for birth registration. He said 143 New Generation MyKads had been issued to the Orang Asli community in Kelantan through the MEKAR Programme, which brings registration services closer to the community.
